questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Western University in Canada as my study destination because I searched and found that they offered some interesting courses. In addition, one of my main motivations for going on an exchange was to improve my academic English and meet people from all around the world. Western University is very multicultural, and I thought that this would also expand my personal understanding and connections with people from other cultures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been an amazing experience to meet so many new people from around the world, live on campus, and study in a new environment. However, it is not very convenient to get out and explore other cities around London, ON, if you don't have a car.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to find the information I needed for arrival. However, there might be a lot of emails sent with different information, so I would recommend flagging the important emails or printing them out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistant from the International and Exchange student facilitators and volunteers the day after I arrived. There was a meeting section for Winter Exchange and international student, which was a good opportunity to ask all the question I had and also meet new people. In the beginning I had a lot of question regarding the courses, which was quickly answered both though E-mail and  in person on their International and Exchange student office. Additionally, because I chose to stay on Campus, I also received assistance with my accommodation and quick overview of the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are several different houses available, but exchange students will most likely get on-campus housing in Alumni House. Alumni House primarily houses exchange and international students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: For exchange students, meal plans are not mandatory (even though it is not mentioned in the housing book). The cooking facilities are good as you share a kitchen in Alumni House with three other people. However, for cooking, you might need to buy the cooking equipment, but you might also be lucky to find equipment that previous students have left. I had a meal plan for two out of four months, and I think cooking by yourself is the best option economically, as you might find friends to cook with during your stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you stay in Alumni House, you might not need to buy a duvet, pillow, and other things for your room before you arrive, as other people leave their things from the previous term. Personally, I saved a lot of money by doing this and just washed everything before use. The heater does not always work in the suite, so it might be necessary to buy a small fan, which can be useful on both warm and cold days. In on-campus housing, they request that you fill out a roommate agreement, which I recommend you do. This could be useful to avoid later disagreements and also set a good foundation for discussing different living styles.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The reception at Alumni House is not open 24/7, and I found the vacuum cleaner provided to be inadequate.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the course registration process to be manageable, but some courses required specific requests and were not available for exchange students. If there was a course I was interested in but couldn't enroll in before arriving, I recommend reaching out to the professor with a motivation letter to see if enrollment is still possible after course start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International and Exchange office was helpful in answering any questions or providing assistance with course registration. The university also has a more user-friendly website for course registration and opportunities.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: On Western University, course grades are not solely based on one exam, but can be determined by several factors, such as midterm exams, attendance, blog posts, and presentations. This was different from what I was used to, as it involved many deadlines.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend registering for a full course load before the exchange start, but if it feels like too much and you have space in your program, don't be afraid to drop one of the courses. The way they study is very different from what I was used to at my previous courses at KU. It's also a good idea to have a backup plan in case you don't get enrolled in one of the courses you wanted or if it turns out to be different from what you expected. If you need help with courses, reach out to the International and Exchange Student office, as they have a good overview of what's possible. Even if you don't meet all the requirements, try to explain why you might be a good fit for the course and why you're interested in it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I feel that the course levels are nearly the same as at home, although it might depend on which course level you take. I found that I already knew some of the content in my courses, but a large part of it was new. I took courses at the 3rd and 4th-year levels and found the level comparable to UCPH. They don't often provide previous exam sets for exam preparation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had two courses that only consisted of lectures, which was very similar to the teaching style at UCPH. The third course was a lab course, which I found to be very different as it consisted of a lot of lab report assignments and attendance. Attendance and professionalism in class were also marked in addition to knowledge. Overall, I really liked the lab course as it focused a lot on the overall understanding and details of the experiments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
3620G: Immunology Laboratory 
- I liked the laboratory part of the course and it's a good way to improve your writing skills.
Physiology 4520b: Stem Cells and Regenerative Medicine
The teachers are really good and interesting topics. The course also includes blog discussions.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: There are a few items that can be more expensive. Firstly, drinks at the clubs tend to be pricier. Secondly, vegetables can also be relatively costly. Lastly, if you don't have a study permit, purchasing a SIM card can be an additional expense.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied because I had free access to the Fitness (Rec center) on Campus, and there are numerous clubs at Western.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A wide variety of activities was available, including social activities for international/exchange students and athletic options due to easy access to the Western Student Recreation Centre.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I highly recommend signing up for the Adventure Club. I enjoyed it because it allowed me to go on several trips such as the Maple Festival, snow tubing, and hiking trips. Attending different trips was easy since you signed up for each one individually, making it convenient to fit into your schedule.
Additionally, I suggest attending the Global Café, an event primarily attended by international and exchange students. It's a great opportunity to meet new people from around the world.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: During spring or fall, consider going on a trip to a Maple syrup farm. You can also explore downtown where you'll find a board game café, market, and other fun activities like escape rooms. If you prefer not to spend too much money, venture outside and explore the nature surrounding the campus. Additionally, keep an eye out for free or affordable events organized by the university. Moreover, I highly recommend participating in different events or activities during the weekdays as they serve as a refreshing study break.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The first month was challenging because the study system at the University of Copenhagen is very different. However, after one month, I found it easier to navigate around campus and the city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I recommend attending the different events at the beginning and signing up for a peer guide. A peer guide is someone who knows the campus and can also be a hangout buddy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One aspect I found challenging was that people don't hug as much as I'm used to in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very friendly, easy to talk to, and extremely helpful if you had any questions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	Western is a multicultural university, providing an excellent opportunity to learn about Canadian culture as well as other cultures.
2.	I appreciate the fact that it's a connected campus, making it convenient to meet up with friends during study breaks, even if they're studying in a different field. The campus offers pleasant outdoor areas and study spaces.
3.	I recommend choosing to live on campus. I really enjoyed the atmosphere in Alumni Hall, and it's easier to hang out in your room or your friends' rooms during the evenings. The meal plan can be expensive, but it's not always mandatory for exchange students. I suggest not signing up for it or canceling it to save money while still being able to eat well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring warm clothes as it gets really cold during the winter.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I made a lot of new friends from different places around the world.
I improved my English-speaking skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had to adapt to a new study system and I proved to myself that I was capable of passing my courses in another country and a different study environment.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
